note: First hand-built row: crime, noir and suspense from Dylan's own unwatched lists, plus two art-house picks.

picks.name: Thief
picks.why: Michael Mann's first feature: a safecracker, one last job, neon and a Tangerine Dream score. Same procedural cool as Sicario. On your Dissolve list since 2014.

picks.name: Miller's Crossing
picks.why: The Coens doing a straight Prohibition gangster noir: loyalty, double-crosses, great dialogue. On your 2014 PopcornTime list.

picks.name: Ace in the Hole
picks.why: Billy Wilder at his most cynical: a reporter keeps a man trapped in a cave to milk the story. Dark the way Chinatown is dark.

picks.name: Drug War
picks.why: Johnnie To's cartel thriller. A cop and a captured dealer working a sting, cold and relentless. Closest thing on your list to Sicario.

picks.name: Investigation of a Citizen Above Suspicion
picks.why: A police chief kills his mistress and leaves clues to prove he can't be caught. Political noir, Ennio Morricone score.

picks.name: Seconds
picks.why: Paranoid sci-fi thriller: a man buys a new identity and slowly realizes the deal's catch. Rock Hudson, James Wong Howe's warped camera.

picks.name: Marnie
picks.why: Hitchcock's psychological thriller about a compulsive thief. You liked Shadow of a Doubt; this is his stranger, thornier side.

picks.name: Riot in Cell Block 11
picks.why: Don Siegel's tight, angry prison-riot film. 80 minutes, no wasted scenes. Good for a short night.

picks.name: Breaking the Waves
picks.why: The Lars von Trier you've been circling for years (Melancholia, Nymphomaniac and The Five Obstructions are all on your lists). Start here. Emotionally brutal.

picks.name: Under the Skin
picks.why: Wildcard: Scarlett Johansson as an alien hunting men in Scotland. Hypnotic and unsettling, more mood than plot. #6 on the Dissolve's decade list.
